title: mkdir -p, touch, rm and rmdir Explained (And the rm -rf Space Mistake) | Linux Zero to Hero Ep 4
description:
There is no Trash on a Linux server. Episode 4 teaches how to create and delete files and folders with mkdir -p, touch, rm -i, rm -r and rmdir, how to build a release folder layout with one command, and how one stray space in rm -rf can delete a whole project.

I'm Shivam Singh Verma, a DevOps & SRE engineer with 5 years of experience building CI/CD pipelines, running cloud infrastructure on AWS & GCP, and managing projects.

📺 Linux Zero to Hero, Episode 4: a free course with new episodes every Saturday at 5 PM IST.

⏱️ Chapters
0:00 Intro
0:22 Recap
0:48 Your toolkit
1:02 mkdir
1:53 touch
2:15 Deleting
3:33 Real SRE story
4:21 Common mistake
5:39 Interview corner
5:55 Quiz

🔑 What you'll learn
• mkdir, mkdir with several names, and quotes for names with spaces
• mkdir -p: create parents and rerun safely; -v to see what was created
• touch: empty files and updating timestamps
• rm vs rmdir vs rm -r, and why rmdir is the safe one
• rm flags: -i, -I, -r, -v, -f
• Building a release layout on an EC2 server with one command
• The stray space in rm -rf build/ * and how echo previews it
• GNU rm and the root folder failsafe

🧾 Cheat sheet (copy & practice)
mkdir demo
mkdir reports logs
mkdir "my reports"
mkdir -p a/b/c
mkdir -pv reports/2026/nov
touch notes.txt
ls -l notes.txt
rm -i notes.txt
rmdir logs
rm -r reports
rm -rv a
mkdir -pv app/releases/v42/{bin,config,logs} app/shared
ls -R app/releases
echo rm -rf build/ *
rm -rf build/*

🎤 Interview question: How do you delete files safely on a production server?

🧠 Quiz: Which command deletes a folder that still contains files? (answer in the comments, reveal in the next episode)

📝 Homework: build a release layout in /tmp with one mkdir -p command, remove it with rm -rv, and comment the folders you created
